current_answer: As of 25 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. Fresh independent evidence is mixed and task-specific: Sonar’s same Java suite puts GPT-6 Sol above GPT-5.6 Sol but below GPT-6 Astra; PolicyBench also puts Sol above GPT-5.6 Sol, with serving and tool-choice caveats; and a ten-task matched comparison finds GPT-6 Luna faster while GPT-5.6 Luna wins more first-pass and review-quality judgments. Reports of omitted items, looping, and different reasoning effort between Codex subscription and an API path are real system leads. Recent provider incidents and unchanged subscription limits keep availability, routing, configuration, pricing, and access separate from capability. Replay a fixed task with release boundary, served identity, route, effort, tools, context, budget, artifact, and control before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: GPT-6 is not one verdict. Independent tests put Sol above its predecessor on one Java suite, while a matched ten-task comparison finds Luna 6 faster but weaker on quality. Consumer/API effort and route differences remain unresolved.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.
Sonar's same Java suite puts GPT-6 Sol above GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5, but below GPT-6 Astra.
PolicyBench also puts GPT-6 Sol above GPT-5.6 Sol, with serving shape, tool-choice, and reference-correction limits.
A ten-task matched comparison finds GPT-6 Luna faster while GPT-5.6 Luna wins more first-pass and review-quality judgments.
Reports of omitted items, looping, and different Codex/API reasoning effort are real system leads, not a universal downgrade proof.
Recent provider incidents and unchanged subscription limits keep availability, access, routing, configuration, pricing, and capability separate.
AI Drift Detector shows the market value of a fixed weekly evaluator; this pool differentiates with a surface, route, budget, and action receipt.
Reader move: replay one fixed task with served identity, release boundary, effort, route, tools, context, budget, artifact, and control before switching.
uncertainty: No representative fixed-task series spans Chat, Work, Codex, API, and competing providers with provider-served identity, route, effort, tools, context, budget, artifact, judge, and denominator.
Sonar and PolicyBench are cross-sectional task suites; the matched Luna report is small and uses one codebase and a same-family judge.
Community reports are self-selected and often lack served-model, route, effort, account, or allowance receipts.
Provider status and pricing records establish declared operational and commercial terms, not account-level task quality or value.
Analytics, a human pilot, a provider ledger, a recovered-work measure, and willingness-to-pay evidence remain unavailable.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 25 September 2026. Independent and matched evidence is mixed; the next decision is a deployed replay with effort and route receipts, not a universal downgrade claim.
